data.confMeta: read it once, then it becomes the permanent record of this day
data.entryText: Aug 18 CM fell $1,840 (14.7%) against the trailing 7-day mean of $12,480. Amazon revised dimensional-weight tiers effective that day, reclassifying 31 SKUs upward at −$2,210 — the products did not change, the tiers did. The 9.11 price slate contributed +$610 on its first full day with realised volume loss of 2.9% against a 4% prediction. Returns (−$240), mix (+$185) and staged ad bids (−$315) all sit inside normal variation. Residual +$130 · 1.0%. Two remediation cards spawned: packaging right-size and pass-through check. This is a recurring daily cost until one of them lands.
data.neverTwice: Once written, a matching variance shape opens with this entry attached rather than as a fresh investigation. That is the whole point of annotating a day that is already understood.

spawned.title: Right-size packaging for 31 reclassified SKUs
spawned.detail: Four of the 31 already sit on the dim-weight candidate list from the last fulfilment sweep. Right-sizing drops them back under the tier boundary instead of paying the new tier daily.

spawned.title: Pass-through check on the 27 non-resizable SKUs
spawned.detail: These cannot be re-boxed, so the fee is either absorbed or passed through. Elasticity and competitive headroom decide which — that question belongs to the repricing flow, not to a variance bridge.

tomorrow.label: The fee change becomes expected
tomorrow.detail: Once annotated, the classifier stops flagging it as unexpected and points at this entry instead.

tomorrow.label: The band still catches the day
tomorrow.detail: A −$2,210 driver keeps the daily move outside the band, so a card still opens tomorrow — correctly. It closes when the remediation lands, not when we get used to it.

tomorrow.label: Both cards report back here
tomorrow.detail: On write, each card carries a link back so its effect lands on this bridge rather than appearing as unexplained lift.
